input: First nine GP29 runes on LP2-15, preserving the visible four-rune/five-rune word split, plus its printed 4x4 square.
key_sources: Five specified 16-number sequences: absolute distance of Fibonacci-indexed primes from 3301 (the printed cells in source spiral order), Fibonacci-indexed primes, each prime minus one, Fibonacci index plus one, and the Fibonacci index.
grid: Take the first nine values in source outward or inward order; reduce modulo 29; decode with C-K, C+K, or K-C. This gives 5 x 2 x 3 = 30 complete two-word outputs, no chosen prefixes.
decision: A case passes only if both complete words, using the exact source GP spelling, occur in the source vocabulary derived from the solved translation and four pinned English corpora.
control: 20,000 seeded uniform-random nine-rune keys under the source subtraction rule, evaluated against the same two-word vocabulary gate. Zero observed hits estimates rarity but does not validate the vocabulary as a cryptographic detector.
limitations: The screen covers only those 30 sequences, the fixed 4+5 header and the source vocabulary. It does not test alternate start positions, square routes, word spelling rules or the body text, and cannot exclude an unrelated cipher.
